Hand Anchor Tool

Mark where each hand holds its item on every frame of every animation: the far arm (the main hand) and the near arm (the off hand), each holding a sword, shield, staff or orb. Click the hand, then drag toward where the item's top should point. Marks and images are saved in this browser, so you can close the page and come back.

1. Character

Choose what the far arm (the main hand, the character's left, behind the body) holds; the near arm's item is chosen per animation in step 2. The item settings (length, grip point, hand size) sit next to the picture in step 3, so you can see the result while you change them.

2. Animations

Choose what the near arm carries first (you can change it for each animation below; the mage: Staff), then pick one or more strips at once. Each file name becomes the animation name (idle.png becomes "idle"). The frame count is guessed from the strip width (512 px per frame, or square frames when the width is not a multiple of 512), and you can fix it below.

3. Mark the hand on each frame

What these meanApplies to the hand chosen above. The main hand's settings are saved per character; the off hand's per animation (its item is chosen in step 2). Length is a share of the frame width (the same 512 px in every animation, so the item keeps its size in taller frames). Grip point is how far down the picture the hand sits (0% is the top, 100% the bottom: a sword is held near its pommel, a shield in its middle). The hand drawn over an item hides where it is held: only the hand's own skin-coloured pixels near the mark are redrawn (Hand size is how far from the mark it looks), so keep the mark on or next to the fist. Turn it off for shields, which cover the hand anyway. The pictures shown are samples, and you can swap them to check another item against the same marks.
← → previous or next frame Q E turn 3 degrees (Shift for 1) W A S D nudge the hand (Shift for finer) T switch between main and off hand F item in front or behind H hide the item on this frame Z X narrower or wider (turned shield) C copy the previous frame 1-9 jump to that animation
Tip for long animations: mark the key frames (every 2 to 4 frames), then press "Fill unmarked frames in between". Filled frames are drawn with a dashed border and are blended from the marks on either side. Fix any that look off by editing them, which turns them into normal marks.

4. Export

"Save this animation" saves only the open character and animation as a .json file named after them (for example warrior_male_idle.json); save it into that animation's folder, or into inbox/. "Save all" saves every character and animation. Name characters like the library folders ("Warrior Male" goes to animations/warrior_male) and animations "idle", "hit" and so on. The export holds every character and animation, with both hands. Positions are fractions of each frame (0 to 1 from the top left). Angle 0 means the item points straight up, and positive turns clockwise. Older exports with one hand load into the main hand.
